info.name: Preservica - storage report (hot and cold)
info.description:
# Storage used, by hot and cold storage

Works out how much storage Rod Library's Preservica content uses in each storage location, and totals it as **Hot** and **Cold**. Preservica doesn't publish a single "storage used" request, so this collection measures it: for every asset it reads each file's size and the storage locations that hold the file, then adds them up. It also lists Preservica's Analytics datasets, in case one of them already reports storage for your system.

**Before you start:** on this collection's **Variables** tab, fill in `username` and `password` in the **Current value** column, then click **Save**. Optional variables:
- `folderRefs`: folder references, separated by commas, to measure only those folders (blank = everything);
- `allGenerations`: `true` (default) counts every stored generation of every file, which is what takes up storage; `false` counts only the current (active) ones;
- `coldPattern`: storage location names matching this count as Cold (default `glacier|deep|cold|archive|tape|offline`; everything else is Hot).

## Steps

1. Click the collection's **⋯** menu > **Run collection**, and click **Run**. It logs in, lists the Analytics datasets, finds every asset, and measures them one at a time (several requests per asset, so a few thousand assets take a while). The **Console** shows progress, e.g. `Measured 120 of 207 assets`.
2. When it finishes, open **5. Show the storage report** and click its response's **Visualize** tab: totals by tier, by storage location, by storage location and representation (Preservation, Access), and by generation, plus a **Download CSV** button.
3. Check the **By storage location** table: each location's tier is guessed from its name. If one is in the wrong tier, change `coldPattern` and send request 5 again; nothing needs measuring again.

## Notes

- A file kept in two locations (say a hot copy and a cold copy) counts in both, because it uses storage in both.
- The figures cover what the logged-in account can see. An account without **Read Metadata** on some records misses those records. Preservica's own billing figures can also include things this doesn't (deleted content awaiting removal, metadata, thumbnails), so treat this as a breakdown of your content, and compare its totals with what Preservica reports for your account.
- **2. List Analytics datasets** shows what reporting datasets your Preservica offers (`GET /api/analytics/datasets`). If one is about storage, its details are in **2b**, and its documentation is on your server at `/api/analytics/documentation.html`.
- Running the collection again starts over: request 3 clears the previous results.

request.description: Measures one asset and moves on to the next: its representations (`/api/entity/information-objects/{ref}/representations`), their content objects, every generation (`/api/entity/content-objects/{ref}/generations`), each file's size (`.../bitstreams/{n}`) and the storage locations holding it (`.../bitstreams/{n}/storage-locations`). The address is filled in automatically; in the Collection Runner it repeats until every asset is done.

exec: const human = n => { let u = 0; while (n >= 1024 && u < units.length - 1) { n /= 1024; u++; } return `${n.toFixed(u ? 2 : 0)} ${units[u]}`; };
const byAdapter = Object.entries(totals.byAdapter || {}).map(([a, t]) => ({ adapter: a, tier: tierOf(a), files: t.files, bytes: t.bytes, size: human(t.bytes) }))
byAdapter.forEach(r => { tiers[r.tier] = tiers[r.tier] || { files: 0, bytes: 0 }; tiers[r.tier].files += r.files; tiers[r.tier].bytes += r.bytes; });
const byTier = Object.entries(tiers).map(([tier, t]) => ({ tier, files: t.files, bytes: t.bytes, size: human(t.bytes) }));
const byRep = Object.entries(totals.byAdapterRep || {}).map(([k, t]) => { const [adapter, rep] = k.split('\t');
return { tier: tierOf(adapter), adapter, representation: rep, files: t.files, bytes: t.bytes, size: human(t.bytes) }; })

exec: // Fetches each step for one asset and shows Preservica's raw answers, so a format
// the collection doesn't recognise can be seen. Nothing is changed.
const send = url => new Promise((ok, fail) => pm.sendRequest({ url, header: { 'Preservica-Access-Token': pm.collectionVariables.get('token') } }, (e, r) => e ? fail(e) : ok(r)));
const show = (name, url, res) => { steps.push({ name, url: url.replace(/^https?:\/\/[^/]+/, ''), code: res.code, body: res.text().slice(0, 4000) });
if (!ref) { console.log('Run the collection once (or put an asset reference in debugAsset) first.'); return; }
const first = (text, re) => { const m = text.match(re); return m ? m[1].trim() : ''; };
const repsXml = show('1 representations', pm.request.url.toString(), pm.response);
const repXml = show('2 representation', repUrl, await send(repUrl));
const gensXml = show('3 generations', gensUrl, await send(gensUrl));
const genXml = show('4 generation', genUrl, await send(genUrl));
} else console.log('Step 4 lists no file addresses the collection recognises: the answer above shows the real layout.');
} else console.log('Step 3 lists no version addresses the collection recognises: the answer above shows the real layout.');
